newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Caltex Philippines says not keen on Iraqi crude.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Philippines says not keen on Iraqi crude.

text.p: Caltex (Philippines) Inc said on Thursday it will not purchase Iraqi crude since it will not result in lower costs, a top company official said.
"We are not ordering Iraqi crude since, based on our study, it will not result in an optimal crude mix," the official who asked not to be named told Reuters.
The same official had said last month that the company was looking at the purchase of Iraqi crude for January and February use.
He added that since the price of Iraqi crude is unchanged, it is unlikely the company will consider buying for March and April.
Caltex Philippines, the local unit of Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture of Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, operates a 72,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery in the northern Philippines.

Another local refiner, Petron Corp, said that it did not consider purchasing of Iraqi crude as the grade does not match with the company's requirements. Furthermore, most of Petron's crude purchases are contracted on a three to five year basis, company officials said.
Officials of Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell group, were not immediately available for comment.
